land.text: the Kingdom of Norway that Denmark 'was forced by the Treaty of Kiel to cede ... to Sweden' in 1814 (Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands stayed Danish)

predecessors.note: Infobox: 'State re-established: 25 February 1814'; the Denmark-Norway dossier ends at the Treaty of Kiel, 14 January 1814.

capitals.name: Christiania (Oslo)
capitals.note: Kingdom of Norway (1814) infobox: capital 'Christiania' (later Oslo). The pages opened do not date the renaming to Oslo.

capitals.name: London (government in exile)
capitals.note: 'King Haakon and the Norwegian government escaped to ... London' after the invasion of 9 April 1940; the page gives no date. The German occupiers governed from Oslo.

capitals.name: Oslo
capitals.note: King Haakon VII returned to Oslo on 7 June 1945 and General Thorne handed power to him that day.

keyframe_review.note: 346,290 km2, mainland Norway including Finnmark. The Norway page gives 323,808 km2 'without' Svalbard and Jan Mayen (modern figure): ratio 1.07. The 1814 pages give no area; they name no frontier except that Denmark kept Greenland, Iceland and the Faroes. Held for 1814 only; Cliopatria has no Norway shape for 1815-1904 because it draws the land inside the United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway (ledger loss and gain).

Same 346,290 km2 shape for 1905-1921, the land of the independent kingdom after the 7 June 1905 declaration (Sweden accepted on 26 October 1905). The Union page does not describe Norway's extent; ratio to the Norway page's 323,808 km2 is 1.07.

correction.text: Mainland Norway plus Jan Mayen; the shape is right for 1922-1924 and Svalbard joins in August 1925 (new keyframe 1925), so its years end in 1924

keyframe_review.note: 346,661 km2: the 1905 shape plus 372 km2, which the gazetteer shows is the island of Jan Mayen (bbox 8.47-8.26W, 70.98-71.11N; page: 377 km2). The page dates the annexation of 'the middle part of the island' to 1922, the whole island to 1926 and its de jure incorporation to 27 February 1930; at the grid's resolution the island is drawn whole from 1922.

correction.text: Mainland Norway, Jan Mayen and Svalbard, from the Svalbard Treaty's entry into force on 14 August 1925

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Svalbard shape begins in 1926 but 'the treaty took effect on 14 August 1925, alongside the Svalbard Act', which 'formally annexed' the archipelago. The 1926 shape is applied back to 1925.

420,734 km2: the 1922 shape plus 63,731 km2 of Svalbard-Bear Island cells (gazetteer bbox 11.3-32.8E, 74.5-80.4N). The page gives 62,045 km2 for the archipelago (61,022 km2 of land), so 346,661 + 62,045 = 408,706 km2 against 420,734 (ratio 1.03).

correction.text: Norway's own territory stays the 1926 shape; the strip of East Greenland between Carlsberg Fjord and Bessel Fjord is claimed, not held in sovereignty, from June 1931 to 5 April 1933 (ledger contest) and not at all in 1934-1935

keyframe_review.note: 462,613 km2: the 1926 shape plus 37,935 km2 (150 cells, bbox 27.7-18.2W, 71.9-76.0N) in East Greenland, matching the page's Erik the Red's Land 'extending from latitude 71 deg 30 min to latitude 75 deg 40 min N'. The page says the Permanent Court of International Justice ruled against Norway on 5 April 1933 and Norway 'abandoned its claim', so Cliopatria's 1934-1935 years are wrong and the strip before that is a contest with Denmark's Greenland, not Norwegian land.

correction.text: Norway's sovereign territory stays this shape through 1944: 'Nazi Germany controlled Norway until the capitulation of German forces in Europe on 8 May 1945', so the mainland is occupied (hatched), not German

keyframe_review.note: 420,361 km2, the 1926 shape within one cell (grid noise). Cliopatria draws 1940 here together with Nazi Germany; the page has a German occupation from 9 April 1940 with a puppet government, 'never annexed', so the mainland is occupied territory of Norway, recorded as occupation events with Nazi Germany. Svalbard and Jan Mayen are not occupied.

correction.text: For 1941-1944 use the 1936 shape: Norway stays a sovereign state with its king and government in London while the mainland is occupied

keyframe_review.note: 371.6 km2, Jan Mayen alone: Cliopatria drops the mainland and Svalbard during the occupation. The Occupation page lists a 'Svalbard garrison' and a 'Jan Mayen garrison' among Norwegian Army units after 1942 and the Jan Mayen page has a garrison from 1941, while the mainland was occupied by Germany (hatched in the ledger), not lost.

420,717 km2 for 1945-2023 against the infobox 385,207 km2 (including Svalbard and Jan Mayen): ratio 1.09. Compared with 1936 it differs by two cells in Finnmark (bbox 21.9-28.9E, 69.1-70.2N), read as grid noise; no page opened records a frontier change in 1945.

Identical to the 1945 shape (420,717 km2). The page also names Bouvet Island and Peter I Island as dependent territories and says Norway 'formally annexed' Queen Maud Land on 12 June 2015; none is in Cliopatria's shape and none is dated on the pages beyond 2015.

region.text: Norway, ceded by Denmark to the King of Sweden at Kiel but refusing to be 'delivered like cattle to a foreign sovereign'

ledger.note: 1814: Norway rises as a kingdom of its own. The Norway page's infobox gives 'State re-established: 25 February 1814'; Denmark had ceded Norway to Sweden by the Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814), the people learned of it on 26 January-2 February (Kingdom of Norway page), the constitution is dated 17 May 1814 and Christian Frederick was elected king that day.

region.text: the Hvaler islands, taken by a Swedish fleet on 27 July, and 'parts of eastern Norway (Østfold)' occupied by Sweden in 1814

ledger.note: 27 July 1814: Sweden invades Norway. 'A Swedish fleet took Hvaler on 27 July, effectively putting Sweden at war with Norway' (the infobox gives 26 July); Swedish forces moved to invade on 29 July. The Union page adds that parts of Østfold were occupied by Sweden.
14 August 1814: the Convention of Moss ends the two-week war with 'a general cease-fire'; Norway was not recognized as having accepted the Treaty of Kiel. Christian Frederick abdicates on 10 October.

region.text: the Kingdom of Norway, which keeps its own constitution, army, navy and treasury inside the union

ledger.note: 4 November 1814: Norway enters the union with Sweden. 'On 4 November 1814 the Storting adopted the constitutional amendments needed for the union' and elected Charles XIII king, 'rather than acknowledging him as such'. It stays 'an independent constitutional monarchy' with 'its own army, navy and treasury'; Cliopatria draws the land as part of the United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway until 1904.

region.text: the Kingdom of Norway, which unilaterally declares the union dissolved

ledger.note: 7 June 1905: the Storting unanimously declares the union with Sweden dissolved. A plebiscite on 13 August 1905 gave 368,392 votes for dissolution and 184 against; the Karlstad agreement of 23 September 1905 set up a neutral zone on both sides of the border and the demolition of Norwegian fortifications there; Sweden accepted the dissolution on 26 October.

18 November 1905: Prince Carl of Denmark accepts the Norwegian throne as Haakon VII (the Union page's lead gives 18 November; its body says he arrived in Norway on 25 November), ending the Swedish-Norwegian crown.

region.text: Jan Mayen, 'the middle part of the island' annexed in 1922

ledger.note: 1922: Norway annexes the middle of Jan Mayen. 'The Norwegian Meteorological Institute annexed the middle part of the island for Norway in 1922' after the League of Nations 'gave Norway jurisdiction over the island' and the first weather station opened in 1921; the whole island was annexed in 1926 and 'on 27 February 1930, the island was made de jure a part of the Kingdom of Norway'.

region.text: the Svalbard archipelago, 'formally annexed' under the Svalbard Act

ledger.note: 14 August 1925: Svalbard becomes Norwegian. The Svalbard Treaty signed on 9 February 1920 'granting full sovereignty to Norway' 'took effect on 14 August 1925, alongside the Svalbard Act and the appointment of the first governor'; the Act 'made Svalbard a full part of the Kingdom of Norway'. The page does not call the archipelago terra nullius before 1920.

region.text: Erik the Red's Land, the strip of East Greenland 'between Carlsberg Fjord in the South and Bessel Fjord in the North', latitude 71 deg 30 min to 75 deg 40 min N

ledger.note: June-July 1931: Norway lays claim to Erik the Red's Land. The Norwegian flag was raised at Myggbukta by Hallvard Devold in June 1931 and 'on 10 July 1931, a Norwegian royal proclamation was issued, claiming Eastern Greenland as Norwegian territory'. The Greenland dossier (Danish colony) records the same contest.

5 April 1933: the Permanent Court of International Justice rules for Denmark ('Territory awarded to Denmark: 5 April 1933'); 'Norway lost and after the ruling it abandoned its claim'. The strip returns to Denmark's Greenland.
1940: the king and government go to London. 'King Haakon and the Norwegian government escaped to ... London' (Norway page, no date); the page lists Josef Terboven as the real ruler in Oslo.
9 April 1940: Germany invades Norway (Operation Weserübung); the occupation 'began on 9 April 1940'. King Haakon and the government escape to London (the page gives no date).
10 June 1940: 'Conventional armed resistance to the German invasion ended on 10 June 1940'; the Norwegian 6th Division surrendered in Northern Norway that day.

June 1940: the German occupation of the mainland is complete; Reichskommissar Josef Terboven took over power by forming his own cabinet on 20 September 1940 and Quisling was 're-instituted as head of state on 20 February 1942' of a 'pro-German puppet government'. The page does not say Norway was annexed. Svalbard and Jan Mayen are not occupied.

8 May 1945: 'Nazi Germany controlled Norway until the capitulation of German forces in Europe on 8 May 1945'; an Allied military mission arrived in Oslo to deliver the conditions and the surrender took effect at midnight.
7 June 1945: King Haakon VII and the royal family arrive in Oslo and General Sir Andrew Thorne transfers power to the King that day; the government returns from London.

wars.name: Swedish-Norwegian War (1814)
wars.outcome: A two-week war: the Swedes took Hvaler on 27 July, the Convention of Moss (14 August) gave 'a general cease-fire' and Christian Frederick abdicated on 10 October; the Storting accepted the union with Sweden on 4 November.
wars.note: The infobox dates the start 26 July, the text 27 July and the invasion 29 July; the page gives no formal end date besides the 14 August cease-fire.

wars.name: Erik the Red's Land

zones.text: East Greenland between Carlsberg Fjord and Bessel Fjord

wars.outcome: No fighting: Norway proclaimed the strip Norwegian on 10 July 1931 and the Permanent Court of International Justice awarded it to Denmark on 5 April 1933; Norway abandoned the claim.
wars.note: Listed because it feeds the contested-land rule; the Danish side is the Greenland colony and the Danish kingdom.

wars.name: Norwegian campaign
wars.outcome: Germany invaded on 9 April 1940; 'conventional armed resistance ... ended on 10 June 1940' and the mainland was occupied until 8 May 1945.
wars.note: The page does not name the Allied forces that fought in Norway, so only the two states are listed.

certainty.note: A kingdom with an old settled land frontier; the pages opened give no surveyed line (the 1905 Karlstad neutral zone is the only frontier text); the Union page does not describe the extent.
Svalbard is defined by the 1920 treaty (in force 1925) and Jan Mayen by the 1930 act; the Greenland strip of 1931-1933 was only claimed and is soft.
Treaty and statutory limits; during 1940-1945 the mainland frontier is unchanged under occupation.

notes: BUDGET: seven pages were opened against the brief's five for this state, because four of the nine Cliopatria shapes (1922, 1926, 1932, 1941) rest on territorial acts that only the Jan Mayen, Svalbard, Erik the Red's Land and Occupation pages date. UNION YEARS: Cliopatria has no Norway shape for 1815-1904 (the land is in the 'United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway' row, which has its own dossier with the matching gain in 1814 and loss in 1905), so the ledger records a loss in November 1814 and a gain in June 1905 against that union; Norway remained a kingdom with its own constitution, army, navy and treasury. The union dossier dates the end October 1905 (Sweden's acceptance on 26 October); the Storting declared the dissolution on 7 June. OCCUPATION: Cliopatria's 1941-1944 shape (Jan Mayen only) and its 1940 overlap with Nazi Germany are replaced by Norway's full shape with occupation events (contest from 9 April 1940, occupation June 1940 to 8 May 1945), matching the nazi-germany dossier's contest_start/contest_end/occupation_start/occupation_end for 'kingdom-of-norway'. GREENLAND: Norway's side of the contest is recorded against 'greenland' (the Danish colony dossier records it against kingdom-of-norway); the Eastern Greenland strip is contested, never Norwegian. JAN MAYEN: Cliopatria draws the whole island from 1922; the page has the middle part in 1922 and the whole island in 1926, de jure 1930. NOT ON THE PAGES: the renaming of Christiania to Oslo (1925), the Svalbard 'terra nullius' wording, reign years of Haakon VII and later kings (no ruler list was opened, so identity.rulers is omitted), Bouvet Island and Peter I Island dates, the Norwegian-Russian frontier of 1826 in Finnmark, the exact date of the Norwegian government's departure for London. Queen Maud Land (annexed 12 June 2015 per the Norway page) and the other Antarctic claims are not drawn. The Norway page lists the monarch as 'Haakon VIII' (ascended 2026) in its infobox text; not used. END: alive, so the end year is Cliopatria's last (2024) and there is no dissolve event.
